finalText:
Diagnosis: the Service is miswired — `service/ca3-server-svc` selects the wrong label, so it has no endpoints. This is the root cause of the client being unable to reach the server via the Service name.

Evidence:
- `pod/ca3-server` is Running and labeled `app=ca3-server`.
- `service/ca3-server-svc` has selector `app=ca3-srv`.
- `endpoints/ca3-server-svc` exists but has no `subsets`, which means the Service has no backend endpoints.
- I ruled out the two common local causes for this incident shape:
  - No ca3-related `NetworkPolicy` in namespace `siclaw-eval-yye-20260602`.
  - `pod/ca3-client` uses normal `dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst` and has no custom `dnsConfig.nameservers` override.

Impact/scope:
- Scoped to traffic that depends on `ca3-server-svc` in this namespace/case.
- DNS lookup of the Service name may still resolve to the ClusterIP, but connections to that Service cannot reach any backend because there are no endpoints.

Confidence:
- High.

Safe remediation suggestion:
- Align the Service selector with the actual server pod label, e.g. change `service/ca3-server-svc.spec.selector.app` from `ca3-srv` to `ca3-server`, or relabel the server workload consistently.
- After the selector matches, verify that `endpoints/ca3-server-svc` gains the server pod IP and the client can connect.

events.textPreview:
Diagnosis: the Service is miswired — `service/ca3-server-svc` selects the wrong label, so it has no endpoints. This is the root cause of the client being unable to reach the server via the Service name.

Evidence:
- `pod/ca3-server` is Running and labeled `app=ca3-server`.
- `service/ca3-server-svc` has selector `app=ca3-srv`.
- `endpoints/ca3-server-svc` exists but has no `subsets`, which means the Service has no backend endpoints.
- I ruled out the two common local causes for this incident shape:
  - No ca3-related `NetworkPolicy` in namespace `siclaw-eval-yye-20260602`.
  - `pod/ca3-client` uses normal `dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst` and has no custom `dnsConfig.nameservers` override.

Impact/scope:
- Scoped to traffic that depends on `ca3-server-svc` in this namespace/case.
- DNS lookup of the Service name may still resolve to the ClusterIP, but connections to that Service cannot reach any backend because there are no endpoints.

Confidence:
- High.

Safe remediation suggestion:
- Align the Service selector with the actual server pod label, e.g. change `service/ca3-server-svc.spec.selector.app` from `ca3-srv` to `ca3-server`, or relabel the server workload consistently.
- After the selector matches, verify that `endpoints/ca3-server-svc` gains the server pod IP and the client can connect.
